sections.title: A) REFERENCE
sections.subtitle: Volver a algo ya mencionado sin repetirlo: this, that, it, those, the former / the latter, such

blocks.heading: THIS / THAT / IT para referirse a una idea entera
blocks.formula: Frase anterior. + THIS / THAT / IT + verbo...
blocks.rule: It, this y that pueden referirse a un sustantivo o a TODA la frase anterior. This suena más cercano: lo usamos cuando vamos a seguir desarrollando la idea. That marca más distancia (algo ya cerrado, o lo que ha dicho otra persona) y es el típico para dar razones: that's why...
examples: Artists now have a vast range of materials. **This** means that they can be much more versatile.
The artist is my cousin and **that's why** I'm here.
I studied biology. **That** allowed me to work in a lab.

compare.label: This · la idea sigue
compare.text: Prices have doubled. **This** has led to a fall in sales, which...

blocks.heading: THESE / THOSE + sustantivo · THOSE WHO / THOSE OF
formulas: THOSE + WHO / WHICH / WITH ... (= the people / the ones)
blocks.rule: These / those + sustantivo retoman algo ya mencionado. Those who... = la gente que... (sin mencionarla antes). Those of... evita repetir un sustantivo plural.
examples: Several experts were consulted. **These experts** agreed that...
**Those who** studied regularly passed the exam.
Our prices are lower than **those of** our competitors.

wrong.bad: The best candidates are these that show they have done their homework.
wrong.good: The best candidates are those that show they have done their homework.

blocks.heading: THE FORMER / THE LATTER
blocks.formula: THE FORMER = el primero · THE LATTER = el segundo (de dos)
blocks.rule: Muy útil en Writing (essays, reports) para referirse a dos opciones sin repetirlas.
examples: We could build a park or a car park. **The former** would benefit families, while **the latter** would only help drivers.
blocks.tip: Solo con DOS elementos. Con más de dos: the first / the last.

blocks.heading: SUCH · THE SAME
formulas: SUCH + (a / an) + sustantivo = de ese tipo
blocks.rule: Such retoma algo dicho antes con el sentido de 'algo así'. The same evita repetir una acción o elección.
examples: He shouted at the referee. **Such behaviour** is unacceptable.
I'd never heard of **such a thing**.
She ordered the fish, and I had **the same**.

sections.title: B) SUBSTITUTION
sections.subtitle: Sustituir palabras por otras: one / ones, do / do so, so / not, so / neither

blocks.heading: ONE / ONES
formulas: ONE = sustantivo contable singular · ONES = plural
THE ONE(S) + who / that / with / in ...
blocks.rule: Sustituyen a un sustantivo CONTABLE ya mencionado. Nunca con incontables.
examples: I've made some sandwiches — would you like **one**?
I strongly recommend **the one** at the National Gallery.
I prefer to wear **an old one**.
I enjoy romantic films, especially **sad ones**.

wrong.bad: There are a few slices of cake left. Take it!
wrong.good: There are a few slices of cake left. Take one!

wrong.bad: I need some milk. Have you got one?
wrong.good: I need some milk. Have you got any? (milk es incontable)

blocks.heading: ANOTHER · THE OTHER(S) · BOTH · EITHER · NEITHER · ALL · NONE
blocks.rule: Another = uno más (de un grupo). The other = el segundo de dos; the others = el resto. Both / either / neither → dos cosas. All / none → más de dos.
examples: One picture showed a girl. **Another** was of the same girl dancing.
Pablo has two houses. One is in São Paulo and **the other** is in Singapore.
He's written two novels and **both** have won prizes. **Neither** is autobiographical.
'Vanilla or chocolate?' '**Either** will be fine.'

blocks.heading: Auxiliares y modales en vez del verbo
blocks.formula: SUJETO + AUX / MODAL  (sin repetir el verbo)
blocks.rule: Usamos el auxiliar del tiempo (do / does / did, have, be, will...) o el modal en lugar de repetir todo el verbo.
examples: Not many people **have read** that book, and I'm one of the few that **have**.
A year ago I couldn't drive a car, but now I **can**.
I really enjoy comedy films, but then I think everyone **does**.
Mary didn't finish the assignment on time, but I **did**.

blocks.heading: DO SO · DO IT · DO THAT
blocks.rule: Do so sustituye a una acción completa (verbo + objeto). Es más formal que do it / do that.
examples: I told my students to hand in the essay on Monday and all of them **did so**.
I used to play tennis, but I haven't **done so** for years.
Anyone wishing to leave early may **do so** after 3 p.m.

blocks.heading: SO / NEITHER / NOR + AUX + SUJETO
formulas: NEITHER / NOR + AUX + SUJETO (= yo tampoco)
blocks.rule: Para mostrar que algo también es así para otra persona. El auxiliar depende del tiempo de la primera frase.
examples: I enjoy science fiction. **So does** my best friend.
I don't think we should buy a car. **Neither does** my wife.
I found it hard at first, and **so did** my friends.

compare.label: So I do · ¡pues es verdad!
compare.text: 'You've got paint on your shirt.' '**So I have**!' (confirmación)

wrong.good: 'I don't like it.' 'Neither do I.' (neither ya es negativo)

blocks.heading: SO / NOT después de think, hope, expect, suppose, believe, guess, be afraid
formulas: think / suppose / expect / hope / guess + SO
blocks.rule: So sustituye a una oración afirmativa; not, a una negativa. Con think, expect, believe y suppose lo normal es negar el verbo (I don't think so). Con hope y be afraid se usa not (I hope not / I'm afraid not).
examples: 'Do you think Real Madrid will win?' 'I **guess so**.'
'Will it rain?' 'I **hope not**.'
'Can you come?' '**I'm afraid not**.'

blocks.heading: IF SO / IF NOT
formulas: IF NOT = si no es así
blocks.rule: Sustituyen a una condición entera que acabamos de mencionar.
examples: Are you free tonight? **If so**, let's have dinner.
We need to submit it by Friday. **If not**, we'll lose the contract.

blocks.heading: Tras AND / BUT / OR
blocks.formula: frase 1 + AND / BUT / OR + (sujeto / aux / verbo omitidos)
blocks.rule: Si el sujeto, el auxiliar o el verbo son los mismos, se pueden omitir en la segunda parte.
examples: He opened the door and **(he)** walked in.
He bought a laptop and **(he bought)** a printer.
She can sing but **(she)** can't dance.

blocks.heading: Pronombre relativo (cuando es objeto)
blocks.rule: Si el relativo es el objeto (detrás viene un sujeto), podemos quitarlo. Si es el sujeto, no.

compare.label: Objeto · se puede omitir
compare.text: The car **(that)** I bought is very fast.

compare.label: Sujeto · NO se omite
compare.text: The man **who** called you is my boss.

blocks.heading: Tras auxiliares y modales
blocks.rule: El auxiliar o el modal se quedan solos. Con tiempos perfectos o pasivos podemos quedarnos con varias partes.
examples: 'Have you finished?' 'Yes, I **have**.'
I thought the meeting would be cancelled, but it **wasn't**.
I didn't go, but I **could have**.
'Has the parcel been sent?' 'It **should have been**.'

blocks.heading: TO solo (infinitivo sin repetir)
blocks.formula: want / would love / used / be able / be allowed + TO
blocks.rule: Con verbos o adjetivos seguidos de to + inf podemos dejar solo el to.
examples: Kim suggested going to the ballet, but I didn't **want to**.
Give me a call later if you're **able to**.
I'd like to help, but I'm not sure I'd be **allowed to**.
I don't play chess now, but I **used to**.

wrong.good: 'Would you like to come?' 'I'd love to.'

blocks.heading: Wh- words solos
blocks.formula: WHO / WHY / WHEN / WHERE / HOW + (resto omitido)
examples: He left early, but I don't know **why**.
Someone left the door open, but I don't know **who**.
We'll meet soon, but I'm not sure **when**.

blocks.heading: Elipsis informal en el Speaking
blocks.rule: En conversación se omiten el sujeto y el auxiliar al principio de la frase. Suena muy natural en el Speaking (¡no en Writing formal!).
examples: **(It)** Sounds good to me.
**(Do you)** Want a coffee?
**(I've)** No idea.
**(Have you)** Been here long?

speaking.structure: In the first picture, [comment]. THIS seems to suggest [idea], whereas in the other one...
speaking.example: In the first picture, the people are working in an open-plan office. This seems to suggest a more collaborative environment, whereas in the other one...
speaking.translation: En la primera foto, [comentario]. Esto parece sugerir [idea], mientras que en la otra...

speaking.structure: 'I think [opinion].' — 'So do I. / Neither do I. / I don't think so, actually.'
speaking.example: 'I think we should prioritise the environment.' — 'So do I. In fact, so do most young people nowadays.'
speaking.translation: 'Creo que [opinión].' — 'Yo también. / Yo tampoco. / La verdad es que yo no lo creo.'

speaking.structure: I certainly hope SO / NOT, but I'm afraid [reason].
speaking.example: Will AI replace teachers? I certainly hope not, but I'm afraid it might if we rely on it too much.
speaking.translation: Espero que sí / que no, pero me temo que [razón].

speaking.structure: Both options have advantages, but the former [...], whereas the latter [...].
speaking.example: Both options have advantages, but the former would be cheaper, whereas the latter would reach more people.
speaking.translation: Las dos opciones tienen ventajas, pero la primera [...], mientras que la segunda [...].

speaking.structure: I haven't [done it] yet, but I'd love TO. / I don't any more, but I used TO.
speaking.example: I haven't tried any extreme sports yet, but I'd love to if I ever get the chance.
speaking.translation: Todavía no lo he hecho, pero me encantaría. / Ya no, pero antes sí.
